name: @jl-0/jira-mcp-server

tools.name: jira_search_issues
tools.description: Search for JIRA issues using JQL (JIRA Query Language). Use this to find issues based on various criteria like project, status, assignee, text content, etc. Returns a summary of matching issues.

jql.description: JQL query string to search for issues. Examples: "project = IDS", "assignee = currentUser() AND status = Open", "key = IDS-10314". IMPORTANT: Use "key = ISSUE-123" to query a specific issue, NOT "text ~ ISSUE-123" which performs unnecessary full-text search.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return as a number (default: 50, max: 100). Must be a number, not a string.

fields.description: Optional array of field names to include. Example: ["summary", "status", "assignee"]. Strongly recommended to specify only needed fields to reduce data transfer. If omitted, returns common fields: summary, status, priority, assignee, reporter, created, updated, issuetype, project, labels, components

expand.description: Optional array of entities to expand. Example: ["changelog", "transitions"]. Common values: changelog, renderedFields, transitions

properties.description: Optional array of issue properties to include. Example: ["prop1", "prop2"]. Use "*all" to include all properties

startAt.description: Starting index for pagination as a number (default: 0). Use for fetching additional pages of results. Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: jira_get_issue
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific JIRA issue by its key (e.g., "IDS-10194"). Returns comprehensive issue details including summary, description, status, assignee, and custom fields. CRITICAL: Always use the fields parameter to request only specific fields needed - requesting all fields or omitting this parameter returns excessive data and may fail. For custom fields, use field discovery workflow first: (1) Get issue type with fields: ["issuetype", "project"], (2) Use jira_get_issue_type_fields to find field names/IDs, (3) Request only needed fields by name or customfield_XXXX ID. Example: fields: ["summary", "customfield_10001", "status"].

issueIdOrKey.description: The JIRA issue ID or key to retrieve. Example: "IDS-10194" or "PROJ-123"

fields.description: Optional array of specific fields to return. Example: ["summary", "status", "description", "assignee", "reporter", "priority"]. If omitted, returns common fields: summary, status, priority, assignee, reporter, created, updated, description, issuetype, project, resolution, resolutiondate, duedate, labels, components, fixVersions, versions

expand.description: Optional array of additional data to expand. Example: ["changelog", "transitions", "renderedFields"]. Warning: Some expand options may significantly increase response size

properties.description: Optional array of issue properties to include. Example: ["prop1", "prop2"]. Use "*all" to include all properties

updateHistory.description: Whether to update the issue's history of views

tools.name: jira_get_issue_comments
tools.description: Get all comments for a specific JIRA issue by its key (e.g., "IDS-10194"). Returns a paginated list of comments with author and timestamp information.

issueIdOrKey.description: The JIRA issue ID or key to get comments for. Example: "IDS-10194"

maxResults.description: Maximum number of comments to return as a number (default: 50). Must be a number, not a string.

startAt.description: Starting index for pagination as a number (default: 0). Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: jira_get_issue_transitions
tools.description: Get available workflow transitions for a JIRA issue by its key (e.g., "IDS-10194"). Shows what status changes are possible for the issue (e.g., Open -> In Progress, In Progress -> Resolved).

issueIdOrKey.description: The JIRA issue ID or key to get transitions for. Example: "IDS-10194"

includeUnavailable.description: Whether to include transitions that are not available to the current user (default: false)

tools.name: jira_list_projects
tools.description: List all JIRA projects accessible to the authenticated user

expand.description: Optional array of additional data to expand. Example: ["description", "lead", "url", "projectKeys"]. Commonly used values: description, lead, url, projectKeys

recent.description: Optional number to return only the N most recent projects. Must be a number, not a string. Example: 10 to get the 10 most recent projects

tools.name: jira_get_project
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific JIRA project

projectIdOrKey.description: The JIRA project ID or key to retrieve. Example: "IDS" or "10000"

expand.description: Optional array of additional data to expand. Example: ["description", "lead", "issueTypes", "components", "versions"]

tools.name: jira_search_projects
tools.description: Search for JIRA projects based on various criteria

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results as a number (default: 50). Must be a number, not a string.

startAt.description: Starting index for pagination as a number (default: 0). Must be a number, not a string.

categoryId.description: Project category ID as a number. Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: jira_get_current_user
tools.description: Get information about the currently authenticated JIRA user

tools.name: jira_get_user
tools.description: Get information about a specific JIRA user by account ID

accountId.description: The account ID of the user

tools.name: jira_search_users
tools.description: Search for JIRA users by query string

query.description: Search query matching display name and email

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results as a number (default: 50). Must be a number, not a string.

startAt.description: Starting index for pagination as a number (default: 0). Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: jira_get_issue_types
tools.description: Get all issue types available for a specific project. Returns issue type metadata including IDs and names. Use this to discover what issue types exist in a project before querying for their specific fields.

projectIdOrKey.description: The JIRA project ID or key to get issue types for. Example: "IDS" or "10000"

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return as a number (default: 50). Must be a number, not a string.

startAt.description: Starting index for pagination as a number (default: 0). Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: jira_get_issue_type_fields
tools.description: Get all fields available for a specific issue type in a project. Returns detailed field metadata including which fields are required, their types, allowed values, and default values. Use this to understand what fields can be queried or set for a specific issue type.

projectIdOrKey.description: The JIRA project ID or key. Example: "IDS" or "10000"

issueTypeId.description: The issue type ID to get fields for. Example: "10001"

maxResults.description: Maximum number of results to return as a number (default: 50). Must be a number, not a string.

startAt.description: Starting index for pagination as a number (default: 0). Must be a number, not a string.

tools.name: jira_get_issue_field_names
tools.description: Get all field IDs and their corresponding names for a specific JIRA issue. This tool retrieves the editmeta for an issue and returns a simplified list of field IDs (like "customfield_25931") mapped to their human-readable names (like "Target start"). Use this when you need to discover what fields are available for a specific issue.

issueIdOrKey.description: The JIRA issue ID or key to get field names for. Example: "IDS-10194" or "PROJ-123"

tools.name: jira_search_issue_fields
tools.description: Search for specific fields by name in a JIRA issue. Provide an issue key and one or more search terms, and this tool will return matching field IDs and names. Supports partial/fuzzy matching - for example, searching for "test" will match "Task Test Procedure". Use this when you need to find the field ID for a specific field name.

issueIdOrKey.description: The JIRA issue ID or key to search fields for. Example: "IDS-10194" or "PROJ-123"

searchTerms.description: Array of search terms to match against field names. Example: ["test", "story points"]. Partial matches are supported.
